repo.description:
### Summary

OAuth access tokens are signed with the same secret as first-party session tokens, and the session
strategy short-circuits on the OAuth marker claim and returns the payload unchanged. Presenting an
OAuth token through the session header therefore bypasses the revocation check, client-existence
check, route allowlist and scope enforcement that apply on the bearer path.

### Details

Every OAuth-specific control lives in the bearer strategy: the revocation lookup, the client-existence check, the route allowlist and `granted_resources` scoping. `GlobalGuard` attempted the JWT strategy first, and that strategy returned the payload as-is when the OAuth marker claim was present, with no database lookup, no blocked-account check and no `token_version` comparison. Routes carrying an `@Acl` decorator refused it, but routes without one were reachable, among them the current-user, profile update and sign-out routes and the storage upload routes. In the Enterprise build, the exchange in `short-lived-token.strategy.ts` that turns a single sign-on token into a session also accepted an OAuth access token, revoked or not, and issued a full session with a refresh token, and the socket handshake in `NocoSocket.ts` accepted it as well. The session strategy, the exchange and the socket handshake now refuse OAuth access tokens, and the socket handshake also checks the user's current token version.

### Impact

A revoked OAuth access token continues to authenticate as its user for the remainder of the token's
lifetime. A third-party integration or MCP client that holds, or has leaked, an access token retains
authenticated write access after the user explicitly revokes the grant, can modify the victim's
profile, and can force a global sign-out at will. The same path bypasses client deletion, the
`granted_resources` scope restrictions, and the password-change revocation introduced for
CVE-2026-53926. Any deployment using OAuth or MCP integrations is affected.

### Credit

This issue was reported by uu K.
repo.summary: Revoked OAuth Access Tokens Accepted as First-Party Sessions
